name: Mark Elworth
bio: Mark "Marky Jr" Elworth is the Libertarian nominee for Colorado's 5th congressional district and is described as a businessman. In 2024 he sought to run as a Libertarian in Colorado's 3rd district, but the state party picked another candidate at a convention he did not attend.
notes: The Libertarian Party of Colorado links only a PDF candidate statement (lpcolorado.org/wp-content/uploads/sites/26/2026/03/Elworth-CD5.pdf), which was not opened under the no-download rule, and no other campaign site was found. He may be the same person as Nebraska Legal Marijuana NOW activist Mark Elworth Jr., but this was not confirmed, so none of that record was used and all ten topics remain unknown.

name: Patty McMahon
current_role: Retired federal employee (U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission)
bio: Patty McMahon is the Libertarian nominee for Colorado's 6th congressional district. Her campaign says she spent 35 years at the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, including work with congressional offices and as Region VIII lead for the White House Initiative on Asian Americans, Native Hawaiians, and Pacific Islanders. She is a Metropolitan State University of Denver graduate and has lived in the district for 26 years.

platform.point: Wants Congress to reclaim its coequal role, defend its power of the purse and carry out real oversight of the executive.
Opposes giving up due process, free expression or privacy in exchange for security or efficiency.
Opposes military action without congressional approval and says wars should be authorized, justified and a last resort.
Proposes a TRUST Act so federal funds are spent as Congress authorized, plus investigations of agency fund transfers.
Proposes O.P.E.N. America, a Department of Education online lifelong-learning system with low-cost accredited courses and transferable credits.
Says she backs a strong defense and respect for allies' sovereignty while opposing wars of choice.
Argues a representative's first duty is to district residents rather than a party, and calls for opening debates to third-party candidates.

liberty.evidence: General statements defending free expression and privacy (speech) against government expansion; no stated positions on abortion, drugs, LGBTQ rights or guns.

security.evidence: General statement opposing giving up due process and privacy protections for security or efficiency.

foreign.evidence: General statements opposing unauthorized military action and wars of choice while supporting a strong defense and relationships with allies.

notes: Read the campaign home, On the Issues and Videos pages and the Libertarian Party of Colorado candidate posts. Her site does not address taxes, social programs, immigration, energy, technology or religion, so those topics remain unknown.
